date_note: KEPCO announced the leak on 22 November and said it confirmed it on 20 November (Newsis, Dailian, Segye Ilbo); no page gives the day of the intrusion.
title: KEPCO says personal data of over one and a half million people leaked from its customer and procurement systems
geo_basis: KEPCO headquarters in Naju; the sources give no location for the affected systems
summary: KEPCO said on 22 November it confirmed on 20 November a leak from its Hanjeon ON platform and SRM procurement system: 152만248 people (over one and a half million) by simple sum, overlap unchecked (Newsis). Exposed: resident registration, bank account and card numbers. Dailian reports KEPCO presumes an outside attacker and has told police; it blocked external IP access and is investigating with the NIS. Yonhap reports KEPCO disclosed a 35,528-person breach a month earlier.
plain: South Korea's power company KEPCO says personal data of over one and a half million people, including ID, bank account and card numbers, leaked from two of its online systems; it presumes an outside attacker.
exec: Personal data from a national utility's customer and supplier systems leaked, including ID, bank and card numbers that can be used for fraud and impersonation.
action: KEPCO urges caution with calls, texts and emails that impersonate KEPCO or come from unclear sources, and runs a dedicated service where customers can check whether their data leaked and report damage.

evidence.quote: 두 시스템에서 개인정보가 유출된 인원은 단순 합산 기준 152만248명이다.
두 시스템의 유출 규모를 합하면 152만248명분에 달한다. 다만 중복 인원 여부는 확인되지 않았다.
한전은 외부 공격자가 두 시스템에 불법 침입해 정보를 탈취한 것으로 추정하고 있다.
한전은 지난 20일 통합고객서비스플랫폼인 '한전ON'과 전자조달시스템(SRM)에서 개인정보 유출 사실을 확인했다고 22일 밝혔다.
has confirmed another data breach involving the personal information of around 1.52 million users
The latest breach came a month after KEPCO disclosed a data breach involving 35,528 people, including current and former employees and workers at partner companies.

validation.note: Newsis, Dailian and Segye Ilbo each report KEPCO's 22 November statement with the same per-system figures and CEO Kim Dong-cheol's apology. KEPCO's own apology notice was not read: home.kepco.co.kr timed out and online.kepco.co.kr reset the connection. No attacker named; Dailian says KEPCO presumes an external attacker. The sources give counts in Korean notation (152만248명 total; Hanjeon ON 65만487명, SRM 86만9761명); the record keeps that notation with words because the figure check cannot read it. The Korea Herald (22 November) adds that KEPCO launched an investigation in cooperation with the National Intelligence Service, relevant government agencies and outside experts. The Korea Times (Yonhap, 22 November) gives the same per-system counts (650,487 KEPCO ON users, 869,761 SRM users) and says KEPCO disclosed a separate breach of 35,528 people a month earlier.

review.note: stronger than the source / misattribution: summary credited the attacker presumption and police referral to the Korea Herald; Dailian says KEPCO presumes an attacker and (with Segye) referred to police; Herald only mentions the NIS investigation.
